title: Comparison for a marked simplicial cylinder
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, the Bergner model homotopy category $h\mathrm{sCat}$, and derived-pushout localization $q:C\to L_WC$ as in [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. Here $W$ is any set of vertex arrows; $\pi_0$ has the same objects and path components of mapping simplicial sets as morphisms. All displayed categories fit in a fixed sufficiently large universe. Let $A$ be a small simplicial category, $V$ a set of its vertex arrows, and $q:A\to L_VA$ its localization unit. Assume explicitly that $\pi_0q$ is essentially surjective. The cartesian product of simplicial categories is the product described in [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-product-parameter]. Let $[1]$ be the discrete walking arrow $t:0\to1$ and $\mathbb J$ the discrete groupoid with two objects and exactly one arrow between each ordered pair. In $A\times[1]$ mark the set
$$U=\{(v,1_0),(v,1_1):v\in V\}\ \cup\ \{(1_a,t):a\in\operatorname{Ob}A\}.$$The functor $q\times([1]\to\mathbb J)$ induces an isomorphism
$$\Phi:L_U(A\times[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(L_VA)\times\mathbb J$$
in $h\mathrm{sCat}$. For $e=0,1$, let $k_e:L_VA\to L_U(A\times[1])$ be induced by the endpoint inclusion. Then $\Phi k_e=\iota_e$ in $h\mathrm{sCat}$, where $\iota_e$ is the corresponding endpoint inclusion into $(L_VA)\times\mathbb J$. This holds without any local Kan, cofibrancy or saturation assumption.
